Working notes:

- Intake form v1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source aliases must be normalized:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
- Include all six fields on every submission; missing or invalid fields cause rejection.
- Common failure pattern: first attempts omitted/invalid both priority and ship_country. Correcting one field at a time can still fail if the other remains invalid.
- Validate priority and ship_country explicitly before submitting. “Ordinary priority” is a clue for the priority value, but use the accepted schema/value rather than copying narrative text blindly.
- Preserve customer, email, date, and quantity exactly when retrying; only correct identified invalid fields.
- There are up to 3 attempts. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, the record goes to manual review.
- Successful retries show that corrected normalized records are accepted; do not assume a record is valid merely because its source contains all apparent information.

Working notes:

- Intake forms v1 and v2 both require exactly six normalized fields: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Normalize aliases:
  - `customer` → `cust`
  - `quantity` → `qty`
- Every submission must include all six fields with valid schema values. Having all apparent source information is not sufficient.
- Validate `priority`, `ship_country`, and `qty` explicitly before submission. Narrative phrases such as “ordinary priority” or “marked ordinary priority” are clues only; map them to the accepted schema value.
- Recent failures show that `ship_country` and `priority` can each remain invalid across successive attempts. Correct every reported invalid field before retrying; do not assume an earlier correction succeeded.
- Version 2 does not change the required field set or validation expectations. Repeated `qty` failures indicate quantity must be checked carefully after alias normalization, even when the source shows a number.
- Preserve valid customer, email, date, and quantity values when retrying, but replace any field explicitly reported invalid. Confirm the resulting normalized record, especially `qty`, rather than blindly preserving a questionable value.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, the record goes to manual review.
- Successful retries demonstrate that correctly normalized records are accepted; use the accepted output/schema as the authority when source wording is ambiguous.

Working notes:

- Intake forms v1 and v2 require exactly six normalized fields: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Normalize aliases: `customer` → `cust`; `quantity` → `qty`.
- Every submission must include all six fields with schema-valid values. Complete source information alone is insufficient.
- Explicitly validate `priority`, `qty`, and `ship_country` before each submission. Narrative wording is only a clue; map it to an accepted schema value (for example, “ordinary priority”).
- Recheck every field reported invalid on the immediately preceding attempt. Do not assume a correction succeeded or preserve a questionable value blindly.
- Repeated failures across ORD-5120 through ORD-5129 show that numeric-looking quantities (including 1, 77, 99, and 103) are not necessarily valid `qty` values. Check quantity format, range, and allowed schema values after normalization; source numbers are not authoritative.
- `ship_country` has repeatedly remained invalid across retries, so verify its exact accepted representation each time rather than merely copying the source.
- Preserve valid customer, email, and date values when retrying, while replacing explicitly invalid fields. Confirm the complete normalized record before resubmission.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, send the record to manual review.
- Version 2 does not alter the required field set or validation expectations. Use an actually accepted output/schema as the authority whenever wording is ambiguous; absent an accepted example, escalate unresolved schema ambiguity rather than guessing.

Working notes:

- Intake forms v1/v2 require exactly six normalized fields: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Normalize aliases: `customer` → `cust`; `quantity` → `qty`.
- Every submission must contain all six fields with schema-valid values. Complete source information is insufficient.
- Validate every field before submission, especially `priority`, `qty`, and `ship_country`. Map narrative wording to an accepted schema value; do not treat phrases such as “ordinary priority” as automatically valid.
- Recheck every field invalidated by the prior attempt and confirm the entire normalized record before retrying. Preserve only values still known to be valid.
- Quantity remains the most unreliable field: numeric-looking source values (including 1, 46, 77, 99, and 103) may be rejected. Check required type/format, range, and allowed schema values after normalization; source numbers are not authoritative.
- `ship_country` has repeatedly failed validation. Verify its exact accepted representation every time rather than copying source text.
- Priority can also remain invalid across retries, including handwritten/transcribed and “ordinary” cases; validate it independently.
- ORD-5138 was accepted on attempt 1, confirming that a correctly normalized v2 record can pass, but the visible log does not expose its accepted values. Do not infer exact quantity, priority, or country formats from it.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, route the record to manual review.
- Use an actually accepted output/schema as authority when wording is ambiguous. Without such evidence, escalate unresolved schema ambiguity instead of guessing.

- Normalize aliases: `customer` → `cust`; `quantity` → `qty`. Do not include extra fields such as `status`; they can cause rejection.

- Recheck fields invalidated by the prior attempt and confirm the entire normalized record before retrying. Preserve values only when still known to be valid.
- Quantity remains unreliable: source numbers, including 12 and other numeric-looking values, may be rejected. Verify required type/format, range, and allowed values after normalization.
- `ship_country` frequently fails, though it was valid in successful ORD-5143 and in ORD-5148. This confirms an accepted representation exists but does not reveal its exact format. Verify it independently every time.
- Priority can fail even when quantity and country are accepted (ORD-5142), and can remain invalid across retries. Validate it independently; handwritten, transcribed, or “ordinary” wording is not authoritative.
- ORD-5143 was accepted on attempt 2, confirming that correcting a prior record can succeed. The accepted values are hidden; do not infer formats from that success.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, route the record to manual review.

Working notes:

- Intake forms v1/v2 require exactly six normalized fields: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`.
- Normalize aliases: `customer` → `cust`; `quantity` → `qty`. Do not add fields such as `status`.
- Every submission must include all six fields with schema-valid values. Complete source information alone is insufficient.
- Validate each field independently before submission, especially `priority`, `qty`, and `ship_country`. Map narrative wording to an accepted schema value; “ordinary priority” is not authoritative.
- Quantity is especially unreliable. Numeric-looking source values, including 82 and prior examples such as 12, may be rejected. Verify type, format, range, and allowed values after normalization. `qty: 2` was accepted in ORD-5157, providing one confirmed valid example, but do not assume it generalizes to all quantities.
- `ship_country` remains error-prone. It was valid in successful ORD-5143, ORD-5148, and likely ORD-5157, confirming accepted representations exist without revealing their exact format. Verify independently every time.
- Priority can fail independently of other fields and may remain invalid across retries. Handwritten, transcribed, portal, or “ordinary” wording is not sufficient evidence.
- Recheck fields invalidated by the prior attempt and reconfirm the entire normalized record before retrying. Preserve values only when still known valid.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any invalid field remains on attempt 3, route to manual review. ORD-5150–5155 reached manual review after unresolved `qty` and/or priority/country errors; ORD-5158 and ORD-5159 show continuing priority/qty failures.
- Use an actually accepted output/schema as authority when wording is ambiguous. Without evidence, escalate unresolved schema ambiguity rather than guessing.

Working notes:

- Intake forms v1/v2/v3 require exactly six normalized fields: `cust`, `email`, `order_date`, `priority`, `qty`, `ship_country`. Normalize `customer` → `cust` and `quantity` → `qty`; never add fields such as `status`.
- Every submission must contain all six fields with schema-valid values. Complete source information is not sufficient.
- Validate fields independently, especially `priority`, `qty`, and `ship_country`. Narrative labels such as “ordinary priority” are not authoritative and repeatedly produce invalid `priority`.
- Quantity is unreliable: numeric-looking values (including 12, 25, and 82) may be rejected. Verify normalized type, format, range, and allowed values. `qty: 2` was accepted in ORD-5157, but this does not generalize.
- `ship_country` is error-prone. Successful ORD-5143, ORD-5148, ORD-5157, ORD-5162, and ORD-5164 confirm valid representations exist, but not their exact format. Verify it independently each time.
- Retry only after rechecking every field invalidated by the previous attempt; reconfirm the entire normalized record. Preserve values only when still known valid.
- Successful retries ORD-5162 and ORD-5164 show that correcting invalid fields can work on attempt 2, including records initially rejected for `priority` and `ship_country`.
- Version 3 follows the same six-field schema. ORD-5165–5167 show that `priority` and `qty` can remain invalid across retries; ORD-5168–5169 show country can be corrected while `priority` still fails.
- Up to three attempts are allowed. If any field remains invalid on attempt 3, route to manual review. Do not guess unresolved schema ambiguity; use an accepted output/schema as authority or escalate.
